question: Following a significant change in leadership at India's premier space agency, which distinguished scientist was appointed as the new Chairman of ISRO and Secretary of the Department of Space in January 2025, succeeding S. Somanath?
solution:
The correct answer is __**V. Narayanan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dr. V. Narayanan is a distinguished scientist at ISRO and has played a crucial role in India's space programs, especially in the domain of rocket propulsion.
 
• He succeeded S. Somanath as the Chairman of ISRO and Secretary of the Department of Space in January 2025.
 
• Dr. Narayanan has been instrumental in the development of cryogenic propulsion systems, including the Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS) for the GSLV rocket.
 
• He led the Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC), which is a vital division of ISRO responsible for the development of liquid propulsion technologies.
 
• Under his leadership, ISRO has achieved significant advancements in rocket technologies and launched several impactful missions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **K. Radhakrishnan**

 
 
• Dr. K. Radhakrishnan is a former Chairman of ISRO who served from 2009 to 2014.
 
• He was instrumental in the successful launch of the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) in 2013, making India the first country to reach Mars in its maiden attempt.
 
• He was honored with the Padma Bhushan in 2014 for his contributions to space science and technology.
 
 
 
• **K. Sivan**
 
 
• Dr. K. Sivan served as the Chairman of ISRO from January 2018 to January 2022.
 
• He played a key role in launching Chandrayaan-2 and several other satellite missions during his tenure.
 
• Dr. Sivan is well-known for his work in designing and developing the PSLV project.
 
 
 
• **S. Sashidhar Sinha**
 
 
• S. Sashidhar Sinha is not associated with ISRO leadership roles or space technology advancements.
 
• This option is irrelevant to the context of ISRO Chairman appointments.
